text:
alex: Heads up — Acadia (potential EHR partner) is asking for EU data residency + SOC2 as part of an EOY close. We need to triage: do we redirect infra work to support residency/SOC2 or keep pushing roadmap features for self-serve growth? RICE-ish calcs would help.
maya: Do we have a firm close date from sales? can we ask for timeline flexibility?
sam: Sales says it’s contingent in the MSA draft. They want a deployment option (EU data) + SOC2 attestation to sign by Dec. Customer ARR is meaningful (~$650k ARR in year 1), but not guaranteed until we deliver.
chen: Quick security notes — SOC2 scope (controls + docs) is org/process heavy: expect 4–6 months prep for a Type I if we prioritize, more for Type II. EU data residency for inference/storage is more engineering: routing, storage segreg, KMS scoping. Rough engineer effort ~6–10 weeks to implement a targeted residency path (carveout) vs 3–4 months to generalize.
lisa: If we pivot infra to this, we push back product OKR: conversational-search and billing improvements which drive self-serve expansion. Those two are high-velocity growth levers.
alex: Quick RICE mental model attempt — Reach: this customer = 1 large account (R=1) but if we generalize to EU customers maybe R=30 in next 12mo. Impact: customer revenue & reference = 8. Confidence: 0.6. Effort: carveout 2 devs x 8wks => E=2 (months). So RICE_carveout ~ (30*8*0.6)/2 = 72. RICE_generalize ~ (30*8*0.6)/4 = 36. (very rough)
maya: Those numbers skew a lot on the "reach" assumption. Need better ARR forecast and how many EU customers on pipeline.
chen: Also consider risk-reduction value: having residency reduces contract friction for regulated customers generally — not purely revenue. That can bump impact.
ev an-legal: From Legal: carveouts are allowed as pilot with contractual carveouts/SCAs but we must be explicit about scope and duration. SOC2: legal needs controls in place before signing extensive warranties.
lisa: Proposal: phased path — A) carveout private EU deployment for Acadia (fast path, isolate infra + KMS), B) run SOC2 readiness in parallel but scope minimal for the customer only, C) plan generalization next quarter if more demand.
sam: Sales likes phased but they need a commitment timeline to report to customer. Can we promise a private EU beta in 8–10 weeks?
chen: 8–10 weeks is doable if we scope carveout tightly: no full console integration initially, just inference and embeddings store + audit logs.
security-bot: NOTE: ensure KMS key separation, audit logging enabled, and access controls documented. Otherwise legal may push back.
evan-legal: Also recommend a time-limited carveout clause and clear acceptance criteria for the customer to avoid unlimited obligations.
alex: Action items: (1) Eng leads — produce an 8wk carveout plan (PRD, rough effort, risks) by Wed. (2) Security/legal — list mandatory SOC2 controls we must have in place for contract sign-off by Wed. (3) Sales — confirm customer deadline and ARR certainty. We'll RICE-rank with numbers and present to exec on Friday.
maya: Agree. If the RICE after real numbers favors carveout -> proceed. If not, we can negotiate staged acceptance with the customer (pilot + delayed SOC2 milestone).
chen: I'll start a short tech spec and ops runbook for the carveout. Happy to sync with eng infra tomorrow.
sam: I'll push to the customer to accept a phased acceptance and get written timeline.
lisa: I'll update OKR board with a potential shift and estimated deltas for Q2.
alex: Thanks — keeping this thread as the single source for updates. Ping me if blockers. :thumbsup:
security-bot: Reminder — create a dedicated ticket for KMS and key separation.
